newsitem.title: USA: FBI warns of child pornography on Internet.
newsitem.headline: FBI warns of child pornography on Internet.

text.p: Pedophiles are increasingly using the Internet to contact children and transmit child pornography, FBI Director Louis Freeh said on Tuesday.

Freeh, testifying at a Senate appropriations subcommittee hearing, called the Internet a wonderful learning tool. But he added: "The dark side of that technology is that criminals and pedophiles can reach into your home. You never know who you are speaking to.
"Increasingly, pedophiles and sexual predators are using the Internet and on-line services to target and recruit victims and to facilitate the distribution of child pornography," he said.
Freeh said pedophiles were using chat rooms and bulletin boards to contact children and were transmitting child pornography by e-mail.
He said the FBI had started an investigation in 1994, called "Innocent Images", to focus on sexual exploitation of children through the Internet, which has led to 83 felony convictions.

"Our highest priority is on those individuals who indicate a willingness to travel for the purpose of engaging in sexual activity with a juvenile and those who are distributors of child pornography," Freeh said.
He said the FBI had consolidated all its investigative operations involving child victimisation in an office of crimes against children to coordinate its efforts.

Congress last year voted to prohibit the transmission of indecent material over the Internet but the law is under review by the U.S. Supreme Court. Opponents say the legislation violates free speech protections.
